q: Financial Review Demands for grants is a requisition in the form of a statement with the estimate of expenditure from-
e: Consolidated Fund of India — that is the right answer. Option (A) is correct: Demands for Grants are the statements of estimated expenditure laid before Parliament, and the expenditure is met from the Consolidated Fund of India, into which all government revenues flow (Article 266). The demands are presented under Article 113, separating expenditure 'charged' on the Fund from expenditure 'voted' by the Lok Sabha. Related exam fact: no money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund except under an Appropriation Act passed under Article 114.

q: For monitoring of high value projects of all government departments including IR through MOSPI, the following two systems are in place-
e: Option (B) is correct: MOSPI monitors high-value projects of all government departments, including Indian Railways, through OCMS — the Online Computerized Monitoring System — and IPMD, its Infrastructure and Project Monitoring Division. This is a concept-clarity question. The right option follows directly from the definition; the wrong ones look plausible only with an approximate recall. Tighten the definition in your revision notes.

q: What is the portal for online monitoring of Railway Budget announcements?
e: e-Samiksha — that is the right answer. Option (C) is correct: e-Samiksha is the online portal used for monitoring the implementation of Railway Budget announcements. It is a real-time follow-up system on which the Railway Board and zonal railways update the action-taken status of each budget proposal. Related exam fact: e-Samiksha was originally designed for monitoring decisions taken at the Prime Minister's review meetings and was later extended to budget and project monitoring across ministries.

q: The Budget Estimates are prepared by the Ministries including Railways, as per guidelines issued by Ministry of Finance in the provision contained in Article-
e: Option (A) is correct: Articles 112 to 116 of the Constitution lay down the Union budget procedure, and the Ministry of Finance issues guidelines under which ministries, including Railways, prepare their Budget Estimates. The key is the precise meaning the question tests: each option describes a closely related but distinct idea, and only one fits the definition exactly. In the exam, such questions reward careful reading of definitions — compare every option against the textbook meaning word by word.

q: According to vide Rule 50 (4) of GFRs, the estimates of Plan Expenditure are processed in consultation with the-
e:
Option (B) is correct: Rule 50(4) of the GFRs provides that estimates of Plan Expenditure are processed in consultation with NITI Aayog, the successor of the Planning Commission. Approach by elimination: strike out the options that contradict the basic principle, and the survivor is your answer. Building this elimination habit speeds up the paper considerably. Remember: Link this to the connected chapter topic; cross-topic twists are common in this exam.
📅 Current as per General Financial Rules 2017, Rule 50(4) (NITI Aayog constituted vide Cabinet Resolution dated 01.01.2015).

q: The Revised Estimates of both Plan and Non-Plan expenditure and Budget Estimates for Non-Plan expenditure, before forwarding to the Budget Division in the Ministry of Finance are scrutinized by the-

options.A: Financial Advisers of Administrative Ministry or Department concerned

e: Option A (Financial Advisers of Administrative Ministry or Department concerned) is the correct choice. Option (A) is correct: under Rule 50(5) of the GFRs, the Revised Estimates of both Plan and Non-Plan expenditure and the Budget Estimates for Non-Plan expenditure are scrutinized by the Financial Advisers of the administrative ministry or department before being forwarded to the Budget Division of the Ministry of Finance. The Financial Adviser checks realism, economy and consistency of the figures.

q: As per Rule 50(2) of GFRs, the expenditure estimates represent the expenditure on account of-

options.B: Loans by the Government and repayment of loans
options.C: Treasury bills and Ways and Means Advances

e: Option (D) is correct: Rule 50(2) of the GFRs states that expenditure estimates represent expenditure on all of the listed accounts — Revenue and Capital, Loans by the Government and repayment of loans, and Treasury bills and Ways and Means Advances. Focus on the exact wording of the question stem: the correct option aligns with the standard definition, while the distractors twist one detail. Training your eye for that one differing word is high-value preparation.

q: The ----under each Sub Head of grant for each month and to end of the month is compared with actual expenditure for further analysis-
e: Option C (Budget Proportionate) is the correct choice. Option (C) is correct: the 'Budget Proportionate' under each sub-head of a grant, for each month and cumulatively to the end of the month, is compared with actual expenditure for analysis. This pro-rata monthly break-up of the annual budget is the yardstick against which spending pace is judged. Related exam fact: this comparison is the working tool of Exchequer Control — it flags sub-heads where expenditure is running ahead of or behind the proportionate provision.

q: Exchequer Control is a self-imposed expenditure discipline by means of a system of day-to-day monitoring of expenditure that the cash content of the -----is not
e: Option A (Budget Allocation) is the correct choice. Option (A) is correct: Exchequer Control is a self-imposed expenditure discipline — a system of day-to-day monitoring of expenditure to ensure that the cash content of the Budget Allocation is not exceeded. It is operated by the administrative ministry itself rather than imposed from outside. Related exam fact: the monthly comparison of budget proportionate with actuals is the main instrument through which Exchequer Control is exercised.

q: Vide Rule 50(4) of GFRs, the estimates of Plan Expenditure are processed in consultation with the-
e:
Option (B) is correct: Rule 50(4) of the GFRs requires Plan Expenditure estimates to be processed in consultation with NITI Aayog — the body that replaced the Planning Commission w.e.f. 01.01.2015. This is a concept-clarity question. The right option follows directly from the definition; the wrong ones look plausible only with an approximate recall. Tighten the definition in your revision notes. Remember: Watch the timeline or sequence in such questions; many errors come from mixing up the order.
Update: the Planning Commission was abolished and replaced by NITI Aayog w.e.f. 01.01.2015, and the Plan/Non-Plan expenditure classification itself was abolished from Budget 2017-18; the question reflects the pre-2015 GFR position. (Source: Cabinet Resolution dated 01.01.2015 constituting NITI Aayog; Budget 2017-18 reforms.)
📅 Current as per General Financial Rules 2017, Rule 50(4) (NITI Aayog constituted vide Cabinet Resolution dated 01.01.2015).

The key is the precise meaning the question tests: each option describes a closely related but distinct idea, and only one fits the definition exactly. q: While Rule 50(2) of GFRs, the expenditure estimates represent the expenditure on account of-

options.B: Loans by the Government and repayment of loans
options.C: Treasury bills and ways and means advances

e: Option (D) is correct: Rule 50(2) of the GFRs defines expenditure estimates as covering every category of government outgo — Revenue and Capital expenditure, Loans given by the Government and repayment of loans, and Treasury bills and Ways and Means Advances. Capital expenditure creates or improves a durable asset (or reduces a liability); it is not consumed within the year, unlike revenue expenditure.

q: Expenditure on New Service or 'New Item' of service for which no provision has been made in the Budget is met through-

options.C: Withdrawl of advance from Contingency Fund of India

e: Option D (Either (b) or (c)) is the correct choice. Option (D) is correct: expenditure on a New Service or a new item of service for which the Budget makes no provision is met either through a Supplementary Grant or by taking an advance from the Contingency Fund of India — hence 'Either (b) or (c)'. In practice the Contingency advance is used for urgent unforeseen needs and is later recouped through a supplementary grant. Related exam fact: Article 115(1) of the Constitution authorizes supplementary, additional and excess grants.

q: After merging of Railway Budget with the central budget, erstwhile demand number 03 to 14 are now-
e: 1-12 Sub Major Head — that is the right answer. Option (B) is correct: after the Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget, the erstwhile railway Demands No. 03 to 14 were renumbered as Sub-Major Heads 1 to 12 under the single Railway demand. Railways is now presented as part of the main budget rather than through separate demands. Related exam fact: the merged presentation shows Railway expenditure under Demand No. 85 of the Ministry of Railways, with Major Head 3075 for ordinary working expenses.

q: Article ----of the Constitution permits obtaining of Supplementary Grant or
e: Option (C) is correct: Article 115(1) of the Constitution permits the President to lay before Parliament a statement showing the estimated amount of supplementary, additional or excess expenditure over the grants already authorized. A supplementary demand is sought when the sanctioned provision proves inadequate or new expenditure becomes necessary during the year. Remember: Remember the underlying principle, not just the sentence: examiners often rephrase the same concept.

q: Which one of the following authorities is/are entrusted with the responsibility of establishing and maintaining a technically sound payment cum accounting system in the departmentalised accounts offices?
e: Department of Expenditure (Ministry of Finance) — that is the right answer. Option (C) is correct: the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, is entrusted with establishing and maintaining a technically sound payment-cum-accounting system in the departmentalised accounts offices. It is the nodal department for government accounting policy. Related exam fact: under the Department of Expenditure functions the Controller General of Accounts, the apex accounting authority for the central government's departmentalised accounting system.

q: All anticipated savings noticed in the grants or appropriation should be surrendered by the departments to the Finance Ministry-

options.B: Before the end of the financial year
options.C: By the dates prescribed by the Finance Ministry

e: By the dates prescribed by the Finance Ministry — that is the right answer. Option (C) is correct: all anticipated savings noticed in grants or appropriations should be surrendered by departments to the Finance Ministry by the dates prescribed by the Finance Ministry. Timely surrender lets the savings be re-appropriated to heads needing more funds instead of lapsing. Related exam fact: surrender of savings is a key budget discipline — it prevents the year-end rush of expenditure and enables realistic Revised Estimates.

q: The guidelines to determine cases of New Services/New Instruments of service are contained in-
e: Option (A) is correct: the guidelines for determining cases of New Services or New Instruments of Service are contained in Annexure 1 to Appendix 3 of the GFRs. These guidelines decide whether a proposal needs a supplementary grant as a 'new service'. A supplementary demand is sought when the sanctioned provision proves inadequate or new expenditure becomes necessary during the year. Remember: Note the exact terminology used — the exam rewards precise vocabulary.

q: Under what rule the provisions for preparation, formulation and submission of the budget to the Parliament are contained in Articles 112 to 116 of the Constitution of
e: GFR Rule 43(3) — that is the right answer. Option (A) is correct: GFR Rule 43(3) provides that the provisions for the preparation, formulation and submission of the budget to Parliament are contained in Articles 112 to 116 of the Constitution. The rule thus links the GFR budget procedure to the constitutional framework. Related exam fact: Articles 112-116 cover, in sequence, the Annual Financial Statement, Demands for Grants, Appropriation Bills, supplementary grants, and votes on account.

q: All Department should obtain from their Heads of Department and other offices under them the monthly departmental figures of expenditure in form GFR 8 by the-
e: The correct answer is 15th of the next month. Option (A) is correct: every department must obtain from its Heads of Department and subordinate offices the monthly departmental figures of expenditure in Form GFR 8 by the 15th of the following month. These figures feed the monthly reconciliation of departmental expenditure with accounts figures. Related exam fact: this monthly reporting is the data backbone of Exchequer Control and of the Revised Estimates exercise.

q: Under Demand No. 85, Major Head 3075-Ordinary working expenses-Sub Major Head 02 is-
e: Repair & Maintenance- Way and Works — that is the right answer. Option (A) is correct: under Demand No. 85, Major Head 3075 (Ordinary Working Expenses), Sub-Major Head 02 is 'Repair and Maintenance — Way and Works', covering track, bridges and buildings maintenance. The 3075 sub-major heads are grouped functionally: 01 general superintendence, 02-05 repair and maintenance by asset class, 07-08 operating expenses, and 09 other working expenses. Related exam fact: Way and Works maintenance is the civil engineering arm's revenue expenditure, distinct from capital works.

q: Under Demand No. 85, Major Head 3075-ordinary working expenses-Sub Major Head 01 is for-
e: Option A (General Superintendent and Services) is the correct choice. Option (A) is correct: Sub-Major Head 01 under Major Head 3075 is 'General Superintendence and Services', covering general administration and supervision costs of operating the railway. It is the first of the functionally grouped sub-major heads under ordinary working expenses. Related exam fact: the repair and maintenance groups follow it as 02 (Way and Works), 03 (Locomotive), 04 (Carriage and Wagons) and 05 (Plant and Equipment).

q: Under Demand No. 85, Major Head 3075-ordinary working expenses-Sub Major Head 04 is-
e: Option (C) is correct: Sub-Major Head 04 is 'Repair and Maintenance — Carriage and Wagons', covering maintenance of coaching and freight rolling stock. q: Under Demand No. 85, Major Head 3075-ordinary working expenses-Sub Major Head 03 is-
e: Option (B) is correct: Sub-Major Head 03 is 'Repair and Maintenance — Locomotive', covering maintenance of locomotives (diesel and electric). It sits between 02 (Way and Works) and 04 (Carriage and Wagons) in the asset-class sequence. Focus on the exact wording of the question stem: the correct option aligns with the standard definition, while the distractors twist one detail. q: Under Demand No. 85, Major Head 3075-ordinary working expenses-Sub Major Head-05 is-
e: The correct answer is Repair & Maintenance-Plant and Equipment. Option (A) is correct: Sub-Major Head 05 is 'Repair and Maintenance — Plant and Equipment', covering maintenance of machinery, plant and equipment other than rolling stock and track. It completes the 02-05 repair and maintenance block under Major Head 3075. Related exam fact: the operating expenses block follows as 07 (Traffic) and 08 (Fuel).

q: Under Demand No. 85, Major Head 3075-ordinary working expenses-Sub Major Head-08 is-
e: Option (C) is correct: Sub-Major Head 08 is 'Operating Expenses — Fuel', covering the cost of fuel (diesel oil and electricity) for train operations. Together with 07 (Traffic), it forms the operating expenses pair under ordinary working expenses. This is a concept-clarity question. The right option follows directly from the definition; the wrong ones look plausible only with an approximate recall. Tighten the definition in your revision notes.

q: Under Demand No. 85, Major Head 3075-ordinary working expenses-Sub Major Head-07 is-
e: Operating Expenses-Traffic — that is the right answer. Option (B) is correct: Sub-Major Head 07 is 'Operating Expenses — Traffic', covering traffic operating costs such as train operations staff and station expenses. It pairs with 08 (Fuel) as the two operating-expense sub-major heads. Related exam fact: traffic operating expenses are distinct from the commercial and transportation earnings side of the accounts.

q: Under Demand No. 85, Major Head 3075-ordinary working expenses-Sub Major Head-09 is-

options.C: PF, Pension and other retirement benefits

e: Sub-Major Head 09 of Major Head 3075 (Ordinary Working Expenses) is Miscellaneous Working Expenses, the residual head for working expenses not covered by the specific Sub-Major Heads 01 to 08.
